voice.refText: Twice a week, you sell your plasma, the pale part of your blood. It's the most the law allows. That's the band. A thin strip you wear across your forehead. While you sleep, it lends your brain to a company. And it pays you, by the hour.

Old woman.describe: A warm, clear female alto: a kind woman in her seventies on a metro platform, a grandmother. Gentle and unhurried, a smile in the voice, crisp clear diction, every word distinct, standard English with no slang.

Min-jun.describe: A bright, light male tenor-baritone: a boy of eighteen, your best friend since you were twelve. Quick, warm and easy, a grin in every word, crisp clear diction, every word distinct, casual modern English.

Clerk.describe: A sleepy male baritone: a convenience-store clerk in his twenties on the night shift. Slow, polite and flat, clear diction under the tiredness.

Ji-yoon.describe: A warm female mezzo: a woman of twenty-four, your older sister, tired from night shifts. Soft and low, gentle and teasing, clear diction, she speaks close and slowly, as if she has all the time in the world for you.

Tae-ho.describe: A flat, cool male baritone: a boy of eighteen, the class rival. Bored and clipped, half a smirk, never looks up from what he is doing, short words.

Teacher.describe: A crisp female alto: a maths teacher in her forties. Precise and dry, one word at a time, kind underneath but never says so.

Kid.describe: A high, bright boy's voice, about six years old, on a bus. Curious and delighted, quick, clear diction, every word distinct, standard English with no slang.

lines.text: The academy, that night. Everyone has a result. The rival stands up before you can.

lines.text: Tae-ho: Backs. Go on, weatherman. Say it again.

lines.text: A hundred backs. Facing the windows. And it's dark outside, so every window is a mirror. A hundred faces in the glass, all looking your way.

lines.text: The card never said a face had to be the right way round.

lines.text: A face in a mirror is still a face. The toilets weren't broken. The one card you can't see was always yours.

lines.text: And the room, in the glass: nearly all teal. Most of them were only ever red at the race, and the race is over.

lines.text: Your best friend? Minus eighty-four. Still. He's glad for you. He also wants to beat you at everything until you both die. That's your best friend.

lines.text: And the rival is back to minus six. Between rivals, that's practically a handshake.

lines.text: Morning. The fridge. Your sister, the jar of brushes, and the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. For the first time, the good news isn't yours.
